query: The Paper-Bird Jam {Somebody's routing charm has gone wrong, and every paper bird in your tower is turning in at your window instead of its own. There are eleven on the sill, and more coming.|The paper-bird jam again. Someone has pinned a sign to your door that says SORTING OFFICE.|The birds know your window now. They queue on the sill like regulars at a counter.} {One is pecking at the glass with real urgency.|Two of them are fighting over the latch.|{season == "winter": They're dusted with frost and shivering.|Rain has smudged half the names on their wings.}} Sort them and send them on {You read wings, untangle a knot of six and send every bird to its proper window. An hour gone, and your eyes ache from the handwriting.|You sort them by tower and floor on your bed and launch them in order. It's dull work, and every one of them arrives.|You sort the queue at speed now, like a postmaster. It's still an hour you meant to spend on something else.} Open the window and shoo them {You fling the window wide and wave your arms. The birds scatter like startled pigeons, and half of them land at the wrong doors. By supper it's been traced to you.|You shoo them out in a great flapping cloud. It's glorious. Two notes end up in the headmistress's tower, and people know whose window they came from.|You open the window and let the flock go where it likes. Wrong doors all over the tower, and a reputation as the leak.}
